To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hybrid control schemes are more effective than PD control for vibration suppression of the flexible manipulator.
the hybrid control schemes of the flexible manipulator can be designed to improve the input tracking performance and to reduce vibrations in the system.

(1) the PD control scheme can effectively control the system for rigid body motion but is not effective for vibration suppression; (2) the input shaper control scheme can effectively suppress the vibration but has a limited ability to control the system for input tracking; (3) the hybrid input shaper and feedback control scheme can provide a good compromise between the two control objectives; and (4) the amplitude polarity of the input shaper can affect the system performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of hybrid controllers to achieve high performance of flexible robot manipulators in the presence of vibration.
the development of hybrid schemes for input shaping and feedback control of flexible manipulators.
the control of the flexible robot manipulator in order to track a reference input while minimizing vibration of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid input shaping and feedback control schemes are effective in reducing vibrations and maintaining input tracking capability of a flexible manipulator.
the positive amplitude input shaper provides better results in the sense of input tracking, vibration reduction and robustness than the other two shapers.
the modified specified negative amplitude (MSNA) input shaper has a better performance in comparison to the specified positive amplitude (SPA) input shaper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hybrid control scheme of PD with positive amplitude input shaper is found to be the best control scheme for the system in terms of the level of vibration reduction and robustness to parameter uncertainty.
the hybrid control scheme is an effective method for the control of flexible link manipulators.

the modified negative shaper has shown to provide the most effective vibration suppression performance in terms of the vibration reduction level, robustness to parameter variations and the time response specification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hybrid input shaping and PD control schemes are very effective for vibration suppression of flexible robots while retaining good input tracking capability.
the positive and modified negative amplitude input shaper schemes can be successfully incorporated with a collocated PD controller for control of the flexible manipulator.
the hybrid control schemes can be used to control flexible manipulator with good performance in terms of input tracking capability and vibration control.
